sources.title: Single-Option Aversion
sources.publisher: Daniel Mochon / Journal of Consumer Research
sources.finding: Laboratory studies describe increased search with a single option and context-dependent increases in selection when alternatives are present.
sources.limitations: No Coke/Pepsi field verification, current retail forecast or universal lift. Full article not reviewed.
sources.rights: metadata and short original paraphrase only; no source full text stored

sources.title: A meta-analysis of extremeness aversion
sources.publisher: Neumann, Böckenholt and Sinha / University of Melbourne author record
sources.finding: Meta-analysis of 142 experimental observations supports middle-option preference with substantial design-related variation.
sources.limitations: No conclusion that two units or a particular discount always wins. Full text and dataset not reviewed.
sources.rights: metadata and short original paraphrase only; no source full text stored

sources.title: The Compromise Effect in Action: Lessons from a Restaurant’s Menu
sources.publisher: Pinger, Ruhmer-Krell and Schumacher / IZA DP 9648
sources.finding: Observational German restaurant data contain a compromise pattern that differs across groups and food categories.
sources.limitations: One restaurant, not random assignment or evidence of added total restaurant demand. Read abstract/introduction and relevant scope, not every regression or appendix.
sources.rights: metadata and short original paraphrase only; no source full text stored

sources.title: Can There Ever Be Too Many Options? A Meta-Analytic Review of Choice Overload
sources.publisher: Scheibehenne, Greifeneder and Todd / author-hosted JCR paper
sources.finding: Across 63 conditions from 50 experiments, average overload effect was near zero with heterogeneity.
sources.limitations: Not evidence that assortment never matters. Abstract and relevant framing inspected; no independent data reanalysis.
sources.rights: metadata and short original paraphrase only; no source full text stored

sources.title: Choice overload: A conceptual review and meta-analysis
sources.publisher: Chernev, Böckenholt and Goodman / Journal of Consumer Psychology
sources.finding: The abstract reports moderators of overload in 99 observations, including difficulty, complexity, uncertainty and decision goal.
sources.limitations: Full article not reviewed; linked correction S06 inspected. Do not approve a numerical benchmark from this abstract.
sources.rights: metadata and short original paraphrase only; no source full text stored

sources.title: Corrigendum to Choice overload: A conceptual review and meta-analysis
sources.publisher: Chernev, Böckenholt and Goodman / Journal of Consumer Psychology
sources.finding: Corrects statistical notation on page 348 of the original article.
sources.limitations: Correction is not a new study; no corrected coefficients are used as CG thresholds.
sources.rights: metadata and short original paraphrase only; no source full text stored

sources.title: Diagnosing Sample Ratio Mismatch in A/B Testing
sources.finding: Allocation mismatch can expose biased experimental data and should be investigated before interpreting treatment results.
sources.limitations: Passing the check does not establish complete experimental validity. Microsoft’s example threshold is not imposed as a CG universal rule.
sources.rights: metadata and short original paraphrase only; no source full text stored

sources.title: Measure ecommerce
sources.finding: Defines ecommerce events and purchase/refund transaction and item references, including currency/value conventions.
sources.limitations: Tagging is not proof of consent, complete attribution or accounting profit. Selected event, purchase and refund sections inspected.
sources.rights: metadata and short original paraphrase only; no source full text stored

sources.title: Eligibility and considerations for using product bundles
sources.finding: Bundle availability depends on component quantities and inventory. Documented compatibility and returns rules matter.
sources.limitations: Specific Shopify implementation, not universal behaviour across commerce stacks; no store capability checked.
sources.rights: metadata and short original paraphrase only; no source full text stored

sources.title: Bringing Dark Patterns to Light
sources.finding: Documents false scarcity/activity, deceptive timers, concealed charges and obstructive cancellation designs.
sources.limitations: US staff report, not South African law. Relevant narrative and taxonomy pages inspected; not every cited enforcement case.
sources.rights: metadata and short original paraphrase only; no source full text stored

sources.title: Guidance Note on Direct Marketing in terms of POPIA
sources.finding: Distinguishes non-customer electronic marketing consent and the conditional existing-customer route.
sources.limitations: Sections 7.2/7.3 and relevant purpose passages inspected. Store-specific legal implementation and later regulatory developments require launch-time review. URL upload directory is not publication date.
sources.rights: metadata and short original paraphrase only; no source full text stored

sources.title: Consumer Protection Act 68 of 2008
sources.finding: Official summary identifies consumer-information standards and restrictions on unfair marketing practices.
sources.limitations: Not a complete current consolidated-law audit; no precise returns, tax or cancellation entitlement is certified here.
sources.rights: metadata and short original paraphrase only; no source full text stored

candidates.title: Retain the no-purchase option in the measurement denominator
candidates.principle: Evaluate whether meaningful alternatives help the decision without assuming everyone will buy.

candidates.title: Intermediate-option evidence is context-dependent
candidates.principle: Do not encode Buy 2 as a universal winner.

candidates.title: Investigate decision complexity, not only option count
candidates.principle: Choose guidance and assortment based on customer knowledge and the buying task.

candidates.title: Require evidence for popularity, scarcity and savings labels
candidates.principle: Store the claim basis, date, scope and approval; never invent the badge.

candidates.title: Evaluate offer contribution across eligible visitors
candidates.principle: Model no purchase, complete cost and mature outcomes; arithmetic is not causal proof.

candidates.title: Verify bundle components and platform restrictions
candidates.principle: Provider-specific stock, shipping and returns contracts must be checked.

candidates.title: Check experimental allocation before interpreting outcomes
candidates.principle: Mismatch should trigger investigation, not a creative winner label.

candidates.title: Preserve purchase and refund identity and semantics
candidates.principle: Use provider event definitions without treating analytics as an accounting ledger.

candidates.title: Keep customer status distinct from marketing eligibility
candidates.principle: Apply purpose, channel, suppression and the applicable customer/consent conditions.

candidates.title: Distinguish annualised exit run rate from period billing
candidates.principle: Test recurring-service economics using a dated customer ramp and explicit costs.
